newsitem.title: GERMANY: German banking assocn says Buba M3 goal cuts risks.
newsitem.headline: German banking assocn says Buba M3 goal cuts risks.

text.p: Germany's banking association (BdB) said on Thursday the Bundesbank's decision to set a two-year corridor for money supply growth would reduce monetary policy risks ahead of the launch of the single European currency.
"The setting of a two-year target underpins the long-term orientation of monetary policy," the BdB said in a statement.
The Bundesbank tightened its M3 monetary supply target to 3.5-6.5 percent from four to seven percent this year, leaving open the final setting of a goal for 1998 until the end of next year.
